action_criteria.expected_evidence: Polyradiculoneuropathy pattern (demyelinating or axonal features, absent F-waves, sural sparing where present); may be normal in the first week; here pure motor axonal with normal sensory potentials
action_criteria.label: Nerve conduction studies and needle EMG
action_criteria.rationale: Nerve conduction studies support the diagnosis and, with normal sensory potentials, separate a pure motor axonal neuropathy from vincristine neurotoxicity, which affects sensory fibres [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Platelets 98 x10^9/L and fibrinogen 1.7 g/L with normal INR and aPTT, above the usual thresholds for lumbar puncture; raised ALT and low albumin mark a higher risk of a severe course
action_criteria.label: Baseline blood tests with coagulation: full blood count, renal function and electrolytes, liver tests, albumin, glucose, CK, INR, aPTT and fibrinogen
action_criteria.rationale: Routine blood tests give the baseline before IVIg [EAN_PNS_2023]; on induction chemotherapy with L-asparaginase, the platelet count and coagulation decide whether the lumbar puncture is safe.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Raised protein (128 mg/dL) with 5 lymphocytes/mm3 and no blasts on cytology: albuminocytological dissociation without CNS leukaemia
action_criteria.label: Lumbar puncture for CSF cell count, protein, glucose and cytology, after platelets and coagulation are checked
action_criteria.rationale: CSF supports the diagnosis and, in ALL, cytology excludes CNS leukaemic infiltration; platelets and fibrinogen on L-asparaginase must be known before the puncture [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No cord compression, cord signal change, leptomeningeal or vertebral leukaemic disease; nerve root enhancement may be seen
action_criteria.label: Optional contrast spine MRI to exclude leukaemic infiltration or compression in a patient with ALL and abrupt quadriplegia
action_criteria.rationale: Abrupt quadriplegia in ALL raises leptomeningeal or epidural leukaemic disease; with normal sensation, areflexia, preserved bladder function and negative CSF cytology the scan is optional.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC in L, % predicted and mL/kg, MIP and MEP, with the trend; ICU-level monitoring if FVC <20 mL/kg or <60% predicted, MIP weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP <40 cmH2O, a fall of more than 30%, or bulbar weakness with weak cough
action_criteria.label: Bedside respiratory function (FVC, MIP, MEP), repeated serially while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Quadriplegia within 48 hours with orthopnoea carries a high risk of respiratory failure; serial FVC, MIP and MEP decide ICU-level monitoring and intubation [Lawn_2001, Walgaard_2010, EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Continuous telemetry with blood pressure monitoring: sinus rhythm 76-108 bpm with intermittent sinus tachycardia, without pauses and blood pressure 108/64 to 148/88 mmHg in the first 24 hours; autonomic instability (rate and blood pressure lability, bradyarrhythmia) requires continued monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.label: Continuous inpatient cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Autonomic dysfunction is common in severe GBS and can cause bradyarrhythmias and blood-pressure lability; monitoring continues while weakness progresses [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Sinus rhythm 98 bpm with normal intervals (QTc 448 ms) and no conduction or repolarisation abnormality: a baseline on daunorubicin while autonomic involvement can still develop
action_criteria.label: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
action_criteria.rationale: A baseline 12-lead ECG screens for autonomic dysrhythmia and conduction abnormality and gives the QTc before treatment [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Fluconazole raises vincristine neurotoxicity through CYP3A4; L-asparaginase lowers fibrinogen and antithrombin (bleeding with the puncture, thrombosis with IVIg); daunorubicin cardiotoxicity; succinylcholine to be avoided
action_criteria.label: Check the induction regimen (vincristine, daunorubicin, prednisone, L-asparaginase), allopurinol and fluconazole for interactions before the lumbar puncture and IVIg or plasma exchange
action_criteria.rationale: The regimen contains a neurotoxic drug with an azole interaction and an agent that disturbs coagulation, which change the lumbar puncture, the choice of IVIg or plasma exchange and the vincristine plan.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on immunotherapy in GBS; not needed for the diagnosis or the treatment decision
action_criteria.label: Optional literature search on IVIg versus plasma exchange in GBS
action_criteria.rationale: Background evidence only; not a clinical step of the work-up.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not give further vincristine while GBS is active.

Do not add corticosteroids for GBS: oral corticosteroids are strongly advised against and IV methylprednisolone is not recommended [EAN_PNS_2023]; the induction prednisone is chemotherapy, not GBS treatment.
Do not use succinylcholine if he needs intubation (risk of hyperkalaemia after denervation).
Do not start IVIg without checking renal function.
required_recommendations: Admit to ICU-level monitoring now: quadriplegia within 48 hours with orthopnoea, EGRIS 6 (onset to admission 2 days, MRC sum score about 18/60, no facial or bulbar weakness), FVC 62% predicted and falling (2.8 to 2.6 L in 6 h), MIP -30 cmH2O. Repeat FVC, MIP and MEP every 2-4 hours and intubate electively if FVC falls below 20 mL/kg (about 1.6 L at 78 kg), MIP becomes weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP falls below 40 cmH2O, bulbar weakness or weak cough appears, or respiratory distress, hypoxaemia or hypercapnia develop [Walgaard_2010, Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

Start IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total, about 31 g/day at 78 kg) now, within 2 weeks of onset, because he cannot walk (GBS disability score 4); IVIg is the practical choice because plasma exchange would further deplete fibrinogen on L-asparaginase and needs central access with platelets 98 x10^9/L [EAN_PNS_2023].
Hold the next vincristine dose and agree with haematology whether to omit or modify it; review fluconazole, which raises vincristine neurotoxicity.
Continuous cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses.

Monitor platelets and fibrinogen daily during L-asparaginase and IVIg, and agree thromboprophylaxis with haematology (both raise thrombotic risk; prophylactic LMWH is usual above platelets 50 x10^9/L) [Leonhard_2019].

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography does not contribute to the neurological diagnosis; daunorubicin cardiotoxicity surveillance follows the haematology protocol.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.

Brain MRI is reserved for encephalopathy, cranial nerve or long-tract signs; the deficit is a pure lower motor neuron quadriparesis with normal cranial nerves and mentation, and CSF cytology addresses CNS leukaemia.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome, AMAN variant (acute motor axonal neuropathy) during ALL induction

differential.key_features: Recent vincristine with fluconazole raises it, but vincristine neurotoxicity is length-dependent and sensory-predominant with paraesthesias; this is a pure motor quadriplegia over 48 hours with normal sensory potentials and CSF protein 128 mg/dL.
ALL raises it, but CSF cytology shows no blasts with 5 cells/mm3, cranial nerves are normal and the deficit is symmetric and lower motor neuron.
Cannot be excluded at presentation; progression beyond 8 weeks or 3 or more treatment-related fluctuations would point to it. Reassess at 8 weeks.
No ICU course or sepsis before onset; onset over 48 hours.

differential.diagnosis: Spinal cord compression from an extramedullary leukaemic deposit
differential.key_features: Arms are involved, sensation and bladder function are normal, reflexes are absent and there is no sensory level.

key_clinical_evidence: The pure motor axonal NCS pattern with normal sensory studies defines AMAN.

Vincristine neuropathy alone cannot explain rapid quadriplegia with CSF dissociation and normal sensory potentials; the chemotherapy may be a permissive immunological trigger rather than the direct mechanism.
In ALL, CSF cytology must exclude leptomeningeal leukaemia before all findings are attributed to GBS; platelets and fibrinogen on L-asparaginase are checked before the lumbar puncture.
Onset to admission of 2 days and an MRC sum score near 18/60 give an EGRIS of 6, a high risk of mechanical ventilation in the first week [Walgaard_2010].

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Vincristine causes a length-dependent sensory-predominant neuropathy that progresses over weeks; a pure motor quadriplegia over 48 hours with normal sensory potentials, an axonal motor NCS and CSF protein 128 mg/dL is AMAN. Vincristine still has to be held.
red_herrings.data_point: Fourth vincristine dose 3 days before onset, with fluconazole
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attributes the whole syndrome to vincristine toxicity and misses GBS.

sequence_constraints.reason: Platelets 98 x10^9/L on induction chemotherapy and L-asparaginase-related hypofibrinogenaemia: the platelet count and coagulation must be known before the lumbar puncture.
Platelets, fibrinogen and liver tests are needed to judge the L-asparaginase and IVIg interactions.

interactions: Vincristine + fluconazole: azole antifungals inhibit CYP3A4 and raise vincristine exposure, increasing neurotoxicity (the label advises caution with CYP3A4 inhibitors).
Vincristine: dose-related motor and sensory axonal neurotoxicity; it adds to any coexisting neuropathy.

L-asparaginase: lowers fibrinogen, antithrombin and other coagulation proteins, with both bleeding and thrombosis risk; IVIg adds a dose-related thrombotic risk, and plasma exchange removes coagulation factors (monitor fibrinogen and platelets).
Daunorubicin: cumulative cardiotoxicity; volume load with IVIg in reduced cardiac function (relative caution).
Prednisone and allopurinol: no interaction with IVIg or plasma exchange.
general.proposed: IVIg or plasma exchange with the induction regimen (vincristine, daunorubicin, prednisone, L-asparaginase), allopurinol and fluconazole
general.summary: Category-level review of the induction regimen, allopurinol and fluconazole against IVIg and plasma exchange.
warnings: Succinylcholine: risk of severe hyperkalaemia in denervated muscle; avoid if intubation is needed.

ecg.interpretation: Sinus rhythm, rate 98. Normal intervals (QTc 448 ms). No acute ST-T wave changes.

labs.interpretation: WBC 14.3 x10^9/L (elevated). Hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL (low). Platelets 98 x10^9/L (low). ALT 64 U/L (elevated). Albumin 3.2 g/dL (low). Fibrinogen 1.7 g/L (low). INR and aPTT within reference ranges. Remaining values within reference ranges.

results.finding: Guidelines for adults with GBS who cannot walk unaided advise IVIg 2 g/kg over 5 days within 2 weeks of onset or plasma exchange within 4 weeks, with no preference between them; corticosteroids are not advised.
A second IVIg course in patients with a poor predicted prognosis did not improve outcome and caused more serious adverse events.

general.summary: IVIg or plasma exchange is advised for adults with GBS unable to walk unaided; neither is preferred, and a second IVIg course is not advised [EAN_PNS_2023, Walgaard_2021].

specialized_test.impression: This is an ABNORMAL study. 1. Unexcitable peroneal and tibial motor nerves bilaterally. 2. Markedly reduced median and ulnar CMAP amplitudes with normal conduction velocities and no conduction slowing in the demyelinating range. 3. Absent lower limb F-waves and H-reflexes. 4. Normal sural and median sensory nerve action potentials. 5. Absent or reduced recruitment without denervation potentials on needle EMG. Pattern consistent with a pure motor axonal polyradiculoneuropathy. Clinical correlation recommended.

metadata.difficulty_description: AMAN during ALL induction chemotherapy: vincristine neuropathy against GBS; the pure motor syndrome with normal sensory NCS and raised CSF protein is the discriminating finding.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 6 required actions, 1 red herring; a neurotoxic chemotherapy that explains part of the picture, coagulation limits on the lumbar puncture and a high EGRIS.
metadata.revision_reason: Reviewer 2 GBS audit: spine MRI is optional and limited to five cases with a concrete cord, traumatic, postoperative or infiltrative alternative; generic hidden MRI reports removed.

patient.chief_complaint: Forty-eight hours of rapidly progressive ascending weakness of all four limbs, 3 days after the fourth vincristine dose of ALL induction, without numbness.

past_medical_history: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, diagnosed 3 months ago; in induction chemotherapy

social_history.living_situation: Lives with wife and two children

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. M. is a 38-year-old man with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia who is in week 4 of induction chemotherapy on an MRC-based protocol with vincristine, daunorubicin, prednisone and L-asparaginase. He received his fourth weekly vincristine dose 3 days ago. Over the past 48 hours he has developed rapidly progressive weakness: first both legs, then over the following 24 hours both arms. He is now unable to lift his legs off the bed. He has no numbness, tingling or pain. He has no dysphagia, diplopia, ptosis or facial weakness, and bladder and bowel function are preserved. He reports mild breathlessness when lying flat since this morning. There was no diarrhoeal illness, respiratory infection or viral prodrome in the preceding weeks.

neurological_exam.additional: Bladder function intact. Paradoxical breathing absent; speaks in full sentences.
neurological_exam.coordination: Cannot assess lower limbs. Upper limb coordination impaired by weakness.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Intact. No facial weakness. No ptosis. Gag preserved.
neurological_exam.motor: Upper limbs: shoulder abduction, elbow flexion and wrist extension 3/5 bilaterally. Lower limbs: hip flexion, knee extension and ankle dorsiflexion 0/5 bilaterally. Neck flexion 4/5.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Absent in all four limbs. Plantar responses mute.
neurological_exam.sensory: Light touch, pinprick, vibration and joint position sense intact in all four limbs.
